subject: Post-call: performance qualification & cost levers — action items
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@clearwave.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: performance qualification & cost levers — action items

Thanks again for taking time this morning — quick recap and the immediate asks so we can scope a targeted perf run. High-level notes from the call:

- ClearWave production goal: interactive recommendations for traders — target p50 latency ~100–150ms, p95 target 400–500ms for the 4–6s long prompts typical of the workflow.
- Expected sustained concurrency: ~80–120 concurrent sessions during US market hours; short bursts to 200 for events.
- Streaming: token-level streaming is required (low tail latency) for progressive updates to the UI.
- Model tolerance: you want to try both a 13B variant for cost-sensitive flows and a 70B-ish variant for higher-quality signals.
- Cost sensitivity: aim to keep incremental inference spend below $0.10 per active session-minute if possible.

Attached is a first-pass SLO matrix (slo_matrix_v1.xlsx) and an outline for a small perf run. Immediate asks:
1) Oliver — can you confirm the 95th-percentile latency allowance (400–500ms) is acceptable for degraded modes?
2) Oliver — can you share a 10–20-example request set (anonymized) that represents your worst-case prompt length and streaming expectations? Sophie if you're on the thread, that sample would help.
3) Ben / Karthik — please draft a short plan with recommended levers (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles, model variant fallback) and a rough cost estimate for 80/150/200 concurrency points.

I’ll sync with procurement on the next steps once we have perf numbers and a recommended config.

Thanks —
Maya Srinivasan
Sr. Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance qualification & cost levers — action items

Thanks Maya — appreciated the clear recap. Quick answers and attachments:

- p95 tolerance: we can accept up to 500ms p95 during normal hours; for major events we'd accept slower p95s if we can guarantee no dropped streams. So 400ms preferred, 500ms acceptable.
- Streaming: token-level streaming is mandatory for the UI; we prefer chunked frames every ~150ms of generation to keep perceived latency low.
- Concurrency: baseline 80, typical market spikes up to 150, extreme peak 200 for <30 minutes.
- Model guidance: start with 13B for low-cost paths, 33B as mid, and 70B for high-quality offline/low-throughput flows. We can accept model fallback if quality degradation is quantified.

Attached a small anonymized sample set (clearwave_sample_20.json) — contains three longer prompts and several short ones to simulate mixed load. It's small; let me know if you need more.

Next steps from our side: Sophie will coordinate the sample set and give you a quick list of tolerance-critical prompts. We want a proposal by end of next week with a suggested perf run cadence.

—Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Platform Engineering, ClearWave AI
oliver@clearwave.ai
Attachment: clearwave_sample_20.json (JSON, 9KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver@clearwave.ai>, Sophie Lin <sophie@tradinglytics.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance qualification & cost levers — action items

Appreciate the detailed sample, Oliver — I reviewed the worst-case prompts. Draft technical plan and tradeoffs below (high-level):

1) Serving topology and latency levers
   - Continuous batching: use small dynamic batching window (2–8ms) for p50 improvements while capping tail impact with adaptive timeouts. Good for 13B and 33B variants; for 70B we reduce batch sizes.
   - KV / prefix caching: store KV cache for repeated context fragments in sessions (saves tokens and reduces compute). Especially effective for your common prompt prefixes.
   - Streaming granularity: tune token flush frequency; aim for 100–200ms delivery windows. This aligns with your 150ms target.

2) Quantization / model footprint
   - Recommend starting with 8-bit quant for 13B/33B to preserve quality with large throughput gains. Use 4-bit (Q4) for the aggressive cost lane but validate on your eval set for any hallucination/regression.
   - For 70B quality paths, keep fp16 for best quality unless quant results validated.

3) Model variants & fallbacks
   - Policy: prefer 13B for low-cost sessions (cheap route), 33B for a mid-tier, 70B pinned to a small set of sessions or offline jobs. Provide automatic fallback to faster variants on overload with a visible quality delta metric.

4) Cost estimate (very rough) — attached sizing_estimate.csv includes ballpark per-token and per-session-minute cost across three concurrency points (80/150/200). Key takeaway: with continuous batching + 8-bit quant for 13B, you can expect ~40–60% cost reduction versus baseline fp16 serving for that model.

Open risks and validation steps:
- Quantization quality regression: we need your eval prompts to run A/B quality checks.
- Streaming tail impact from batching: we'll run a 24-hour stress run with mixed traffic to measure p95 tails.

Action items I’ll own: prepare perf job configs for 13B/33B (8-bit) and 70B (fp16) and a 24h stress plan. ETA: proposal and perf job configs by Thursday 26 Nov.

Attachment: sizing_estimate.csv (CSV, 6KB); quant_profiles_notes.pdf (PDF, 8KB)

Thanks all — quick summary and next steps (owners & ETA):

1) Karthik (owner) — run the proposed 24h stress run across 13B (8-bit), 33B (8-bit), and 70B (fp16). Deliverable: perf report with p50/p95/p99, throughput curves, and cost per session-minute. ETA: Thursday 26 Nov.
2) Maya (owner) — coordinate procurement/scoping for the reserved capacity window if the perf numbers look good; prepare a short commercial proposal. ETA: Mon 30 Nov (dependent on perf results). HubSpot link added: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/clearwave
3) Oliver / Sophie (owner) — provide 2 additional anonymized high-tail prompts and mark any prompts that are quality-critical. ETA: Tue 24 Nov.
4) Ben (owner) — prepare an ROI slide (1–2 slides) showing cost vs latency tradeoffs for the three model lanes. ETA: Fri 27 Nov.

We will use automatic KV caching and dynamic batching by default; quantization lanes will be validated against the eval set and rolled out conservatively. If perf shows p95 >500ms for the 13B lane under typical load, we will reduce batch window and increase instance count.

Please confirm the owners and timing. If all good, I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up for Thu 26 Nov to review the perf report.

Thanks —
Maya
Sr. Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com
